summary: Thames River range lights at Lighthouse Cove, Lake St. Clair: a stone tower kept by the Cartier family from 1838 to 1950. Build dates disagree (1815 to 1837).

light.note: Lamp and lens history in the story comes from LighthouseFriends; the record's current light (Fl R 5s, 6.1 m, 6 nm) is not confirmed by any source read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1815 (Lakeshore), 1818 (marker, LTVCA, Rowlett) and 1837 (LighthouseFriends, DCB). The Dictionary says the lighthouse was still under construction in 1837, which fits the later date for the stone tower. The earlier dates may refer to a first or predecessor tower. Not settled by any source read.

notes_for_editor: 1) First light: the record's first_lit 1810 comes from Rowlett's 'station established 1810'. No source read gives a first lighting date; the marker and Lakeshore describe a wooden tower destroyed in the War of 1812. 2) Build dates disagree (1815, 1818, 1837); the story says so. 3) Family span: LighthouseFriends says 'over 110 years' and the LTVCA says 'over 130 years'; 1838 to 1950 is 112 years, so the story avoids both. 4) The 1906 keeper list gives H. J. Cartier against Thames River. Checked on the page image (scan p. 333, printed p. 252) on 2026-10-27: the name and the station sit on one printed row of the table. The same pairing also appears on one OCR line in the 1904, 1906-07 and 1907 reports. LighthouseFriends names Henry Joseph Cartier at this station. Not confirmed by a second report of the same year. 5) LighthouseFriends' light data (rear: fixed red, 16 m, 11 M; front: Iso red 4 s, 8.8 m, 6 M) differs from the record's Fl R 5s, 6.1 m, 6 nm; not used. Rowlett says the light was dropped from the CCG list; the record still gives CCG I712. Check against the current List of Lights before editing the record. 6) The ipl.org photographic page turned up in search but returned no text to the reader; not used. 7) Heritage listing year (record: 2002) is not in any source read. 8) The HMDB transcription spells the keeper family name differently; the story does not quote that line. 9) LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it, with short quotes only in the evidence.
